biography.plain_text: Aristotle Onassis was a Greek shipping entrepreneur who built his fortune through an international tanker fleet. Displaced from Smyrna, he began trading tobacco in Argentina with capital and commercial connections from his father and uncle. He subsequently built an international shipping business and developed Olympic Airways into an intercontinental carrier.

long_biography.plain_text:
Aristotle Onassis expanded his shipping business by matching new vessels with long-term commitments from major oil companies. Charter income supported bank borrowing, allowing him to order larger tankers without financing their entire cost himself. He placed substantial orders with German and later Japanese shipyards, using scale to reduce the cost of carrying oil.

His will gave that commercial enterprise a continuing public purpose. After the death of his son Alexander, he directed that part of his fortune establish a foundation in his memory. Its business and public-benefit activities were separated: a share of investment profits would finance charitable work, while the remainder would be reinvested to sustain the income-producing assets.
